name: muto-atlas
description: Ground truth for FiveM/GTA V development. 24 offline data layers built from YOUR OWN GTA V install and FiveM server: 7191 natives with apiset resolution and a Lua linter, 316k archetypes from ytyp (door type, pivot, physics), 3M world placements, vanilla animation and clip names, skeleton bone tags, vehicles, weapon components, ped metadata, MLO interiors, IPLs, labelled world objects with rotation, 72k embedded lights, 1087 timecycle modifiers, 17 weather cycles, and an index of the QBCore/Qbox/ESX/ox framework API so missing exports and events are caught before runtime. It checks YOUR files before the game sees them: doctor catches silent failures in ytyp/MLO/ydr/yft, diff compares which nodes exist against a vanilla counterpart, timecycle explains why an interior is dark. It edits prop lights against the measured vanilla distribution over 72539 embedded lights and refuses a write whose light count does not read back. Knowledge is organised as a trunk/branch/leaf tree: the trunk holds the rules that hold everywhere (engine invariants, a single tool-trap catalogue for Sollumz/Blender/CodeWalker/PowerShell/FiveM, the verification ladder, flag tables, bone-tag rules); 6 branches (map, prop, clothing, particle, look, vehicle) carry category-wide rules and one slash command each; 31 leaves carry one task each. Nothing is guessed; every answer cites data, and a file that could not be inspected is never reported as clean.
